Join Zoom Meeting https://us02web.zoom.us/j/84837730068?pwd=b3RWS012NWtTYStJM0JuWUovQS8zQT09 Meeting ID: 848 3773 0068 Passcode: 756469 Inviting author/champion/proponent/alternate proposal for EIP-2935 <@!489256758989029405><@!273808422753796097> <@!259648573401071617> , for EIP-2718 and EIP-2972 <@!301186049323958275> Anyone available from <@&688090867927482525> <@&652918665943056397> ? Hi, sorry, just joined Regarding transaction types there was this collection of proposals (and an attempt to merge them into a simple system): https://notes.ethereum.org/@axic/Hyrc1i7ED I did not take it further (yet) to make an EIP, because focusing on rich transactions seemed like an intriguing idea. I'm still mildly in favor of Rich Transactions over AA. While I get that AA is the more complete solution, it comes with *soooo* much more complexity and risks (DoS). By having gas payment and signing outside, but otherwise allowing addresses to execute code directly (e.g., delegate call) we get rid of almost all of the complexity of AA while retaining *most* of the benefits. although I agree that there is more risk to AA there is much more reward, and i think the latest iteration (EIP-2938) is actually rather elegant my personal preference is to start with sponsored tx + wallet contracts + relayers as it is the most minimal change to achieve "rich txs" The latest iteration does mitigate the risks to some extent, I believe the complexity is still pretty high compared to rich transactions. I think the biggest win of AA is "contract pays fees", and as someone who uses a contract wallet I can say that such a feature would be nice. However, needing to have some gas money on my signer is not particularly onerous either, and certainly far from the biggest pain point I run into. what are your thoughts on sponsored tx + wallet contract + relayers vs. rich txs? What is "wallet contract"? My current favorite is Rich + flags + sponsorship I think. gnosis safe, argent, etc Where "flags" means accesslist/expiry at the moment. I very much dislike like the *current* "meta-transaction" thing people are doing. In my experience, needing ETH for gas is not the giant UX hurdle that everyone seems to think it is. That is, there are *many* other problems that users run into at a higher frequency. I believe the counter-argument to that is that we just aren't seeing the users who would have this problem because they never use Ethereum in the first place. Also, sponsored transactions solves that problem *better* IMO. <@!211091239112671234> I think EIP-2929 should have test cases for CREATE and CREATE2 since their address warming is called out in the spec. Breakout-room Meeting 3 (summary) - https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/208#issuecomment-696215635 Yes, there are a lot of cases that should be made into tests -- I picked the low hanging ones first off - those that didn't require any calls or prestate Yea, getting a cold read for another account really requires prestate. Re EIP-2929, does the list of state results https://gist.github.com/holiman/8f54f24008b57d303c92f24732a14943 include the most recent Geth? Unless I turn off the pre-warmup (comment out https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/pull/1387/files#diff-79e6df6e2f3ed1c5f93b381229062582R324-R325) I don't get the match. but when the access-list start empty I get matching hashes. Here's a trace of stArgsZeroOneBalance/addNonConst.json https://gist.github.com/shemnon/b65ff4bd1898c8cd842ce23111ab7125
